title: 耶鲁研究员：马斯克用财富左右政治，慈善捐赠不足0.1%
speaker: William D. Cohan

segments.en: He bought Twitter, now X. He kind of controls the way that we talk and communicate with one another at least some of us.
segments.zh: 他收购了推特（现X），某种程度上控制着我们彼此交流的方式——至少对部分人而言。

segments.en: He spent an awful lot of money on the last election.
segments.zh: 他在上次选举中投入了巨额资金。

segments.en: He intends to do so on the next election.
segments.zh: 他打算在下一次选举中继续这么做。

segments.en: Talk a bit about the way in which a person of his means and gets a singular thing where somebody who has the amount of money that he has can wield influence.
segments.zh: 谈谈像他这样拥有巨额财富的人，如何能够施加影响力。

segments.en: Not just on building libraries, civic life, artistic life in this country, but can really kind of change the way that power is controlled in a country like the US.
segments.zh: 不仅仅是建设图书馆、公民生活、艺术生活，而是真正改变像美国这样的国家中权力被控制的方式。

segments.en: Yeah, I mean, and the scale of that is it's kind of hard to process.
segments.zh: 是的，这种规模令人难以想象。

segments.en: I mean, the way I was thinking about it last night is Sergei Brenn is the second wealthiest person in the world.
segments.zh: 昨晚我想到，谢尔盖·布林是世界第二富有的人。

segments.en: And you and I are much, much, much closer to Sergei Brenn than Sergei Brenn is Delana.
segments.zh: 而你我和谢尔盖·布林之间的差距，远小于谢尔盖·布林与马斯克之间的差距。

segments.en: Cheers me, God, I'm to hear that.
I think that makes me feel worse.
segments.zh: 我觉得这让我感觉更糟了。

segments.en: So, you know, sort of in the Andrew Carnegie tradition for the United States, people of this kind of wealth, like we sort of expected to give lots of charity.
segments.zh: 在美国，像安德鲁·卡内基那样的传统，拥有这种财富的人通常被期望进行大量慈善捐赠。

segments.en: So you said libraries, universities, things like that must doesn't do that, right?
segments.zh: 所以你说图书馆、大学之类的，马斯克并没有这样做，对吧？

segments.en: Must total charitable giving looks like something well under 0.1% of his total of his total net worth.
segments.zh: 马斯克的慈善捐赠总额远低于其净资产的0.1%。

segments.en: So what you're seeing is what you can buy with power is one way to put it is the most expensive Senate race in history.
segments.zh: 所以你所看到的是，用权力可以买到的东西——可以说是有史以来最昂贵的参议院竞选。
